findings.claim: scorecard-index.schema.json has no if/then/else conditional validation for status-dependent fields. The schema description documents fields as 'Present iff status == verified' (verdict, rule_counts, waivers_aggregate, rule_config_aggregate, scp_version, ref, last_emit_emitted_at) and 'Present iff status in (verification_failure, unreachable, no_emit)' (error), but all these fields are simply optional properties with no conditional enforcement. A schema-valid index row can carry verdict + rule_counts with status: no_emit, or omit verdict entirely with status: verified, without any schema rejection.
findings.evidence: schemas/scorecard-index.schema.json lines 42-125: last_emit_run_id, last_emit_commit, last_emit_emitted_at, verdict, rule_counts, waivers_aggregate, rule_config_aggregate, scp_version, ref, error are all declared as optional properties with no 'if'/'then'/'else' siblings. The adopter item object (lines 29-127) has 'required': ['repo', 'status'] only. Schema description strings (e.g. line 43: 'Present iff status in (verified, verification_failure)', line 53: 'Present iff status == verified', line 122: 'Present iff status in (verification_failure, unreachable, no_emit)') document invariants that the schema itself cannot enforce.
findings.impact: The schema fails to machine-enforce its documented conditional presence invariants. Future index generation code, tooling, or hand-crafted index edits can produce semantically wrong rows (e.g. a no_emit row advertising a verdict, or a verified row carrying an error string without rule_counts) that pass schema validation. The 023D markdown report generator and MCP method (both downstream consumers of the index per the plan-doc) cannot rely on schema validation to guarantee the field presence contract — they must implement their own defensive checks. The waiver-content exclusion test (test_index_excludes_waiver_content) does not exercise this gap.
findings.mitigation: Add JSON Schema 2020-12 if/then conditional branches on the adopter item object. Minimal form: (1) if status == 'verified': then require verdict, rule_counts, waivers_aggregate, rule_config_aggregate, scp_version, ref, last_emit_emitted_at; unevaluatedProperties / not-error clause if desired. (2) if status in {verification_failure, unreachable, no_emit}: then require error. (3) Remove last_emit_emitted_at, verdict, rule_counts, waivers_aggregate, rule_config_aggregate, scp_version, ref from required in the verified branch only; they remain optional in other branches. File as TF-023C-003 if deferring to a schema-refinement pass; inline fix is ~30 lines of additional JSON Schema.

findings.claim: The scorecard-index.schema.json status enum description is inconsistent with the implementation in two ways: (a) the description maps 'unreachable' to 'gh run download failed' and 'no_emit' to 'no green run found', but the code uses 'unreachable' for gh run list failure and 'no_emit' for gh run download failure; (b) last_emit_run_id and last_emit_commit are set on the row before the download attempt, so no_emit rows from download failure carry these fields, contradicting the description 'Present iff status in (verified, verification_failure)'.
findings.evidence: schemas/scorecard-index.schema.json lines 38-41 status description: 'unreachable = gh run download failed (deleted repo / rate limit / network). no_emit = no green policy-check run found within last 7 days OR run had no scorecard-emit artifact.' Workflow lines 151-160: subprocess.TimeoutExpired or FileNotFoundError or non-zero gh run list returncode → row['status'] = 'unreachable'. Lines 179-199: gh run download returncode != 0 → row['status'] = 'no_emit'. Lines 173-175: row['last_emit_run_id'] = run_id_adopter and row['last_emit_commit'] = head_sha are set BEFORE the download block; therefore no_emit rows from download failure always carry these fields. Schema description line 43: last_emit_run_id 'Present iff status in (verified, verification_failure)'. The dispatch note correctly specifies (i) gh run list timeout/error → unreachable; (iii) gh run download fail → no_emit — the code matches the dispatch note but the schema description does not.
findings.impact: An operator diagnosing a no_emit row expects (per schema) that the run was reachable and had no emit artifact. They would not expect a download failure to produce no_emit, so they would not investigate the download path. Conversely, they would expect unreachable to indicate download failure, so they may incorrectly diagnose gh run list network issues as download failures. The schema description is the primary human-readable contract for index consumers (023D report generator, MCP method); both will inherit the wrong diagnostic framing. Additionally, no_emit rows from download failure carry last_emit_run_id / last_emit_commit which the description says should not appear on no_emit rows, producing schema-description-invalid rows that nonetheless pass schema validation.
findings.mitigation: Update the status enum description in scorecard-index.schema.json to accurately reflect the implementation: 'unreachable = gh run list failed (network error, timeout, or non-zero exit — adopter repo is unreachable or rate-limited at the run-list step). verification_failure = emit fetched but gh attestation verify --signer-workflow failed OR emit schema validation failed. no_emit = gh run list found no green policy-check.yml run on the default branch, OR gh run download failed (adopter did not publish scorecard-emit artifact or it was pruned). verified = emit fetched + OIDC attestation verified + schema-valid.' Update last_emit_run_id and last_emit_commit descriptions: 'Present when gh run list identified a run; absent only when gh run list found no green runs (no_emit from the no-runs path). Present for status: verified, verification_failure, and no_emit from download failure.' These are description-only corrections — no code changes needed. File as TF-023C-002 if deferring, but these are low-cost inline edits.

findings.claim: The index fixture set covers only status: verified (single-verified-index) and status: verification_failure (single-failure-index). Status values 'unreachable' and 'no_emit' are never exercised by test_index_validates_against_schema or test_index_excludes_waiver_content, leaving two of the four status enum values without fixture coverage.
findings.evidence: tests/scorecard-aggregator/fixtures/ contains: empty-index/ (adopters: []), single-verified-index/ (status: verified), single-failure-index/ (status: verification_failure). No fixture for status: unreachable or status: no_emit. test_index_validates_against_schema is parametrized by _collect_fixture_dirs('index.json') which returns exactly these three directories (11 total tests: 3 registry + 3 index-validate + 3 waiver-exclude + 2 live). The no_emit case from download failure (which carries last_emit_run_id + last_emit_commit per MAJ-002 analysis) is also not represented.
findings.mitigation: Add tests/scorecard-aggregator/fixtures/single-unreachable-index/index.json (one adopter with status: unreachable, error: 'gh run list exited 1: ...', no emit fields) and tests/scorecard-aggregator/fixtures/single-no-emit-index/index.json (one adopter with status: no_emit, error: '...', last_emit_run_id + last_emit_commit set to model the download-failure path per MAJ-002 corrected description). This raises the test count from 11 to 15 (3 registry + 5 index-validate + 5 waiver-exclude + 2 live). File as TF-023C-004.

findings.claim: last_emit_commit is silently omitted when head_sha from gh run list does not match the 40-char hex pattern, with no error annotation, no status downgrade, and no field recording the malformed value. This violates the fail-loudly discipline established across the estate.
findings.evidence: Workflow lines 174-175: 'if re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}", head_sha): row["last_emit_commit"] = head_sha' — no else branch. If head_sha is empty, truncated, or malformed, last_emit_commit is absent from the row with no indication that it was dropped. The emit_error() helper (line 100-102) is available but unused at this site. In practice GitHub's gh run list --json headSha always returns a valid 40-char hex string, so this is low-probability; however the silent omission diverges from the estate's explicit fail-loudly posture (the aggregator's own design comment at line 26: 'never silently dropped').
findings.mitigation: Add an else branch after line 175: if head_sha is non-empty but doesn't match the pattern, set row['status'] = 'verification_failure' and row['error'] = f'malformed headSha from gh run list (expected 40-char hex): {head_sha!r}', then append and continue. If head_sha is empty (field absent from API response), treat identically. This converts a silent audit-trail gap into a loud, diagnosable failure row. File as TF-023C-005.

findings.claim: The in-memory index schema validation at lines 267-271 is not wrapped in a try/except, so a ValidationError produces an unhandled Python exception traceback without a ::error GitHub Actions annotation. The step fails loudly (non-zero exit via unhandled exception), which is correct, but the root cause is harder to surface in the Actions UI.
findings.evidence: Workflow lines 267-271: jsonschema.Draft202012Validator(index_schema, format_checker=jsonschema.FormatChecker()).validate(index) is called bare, with no surrounding try/except. The emit_error() helper defined at lines 100-102 is the established pattern for annotated failures (used at line 105 for missing registry). All other error paths in the aggregator use explicit row['error'] strings or emit_error(); the index validation failure is the only site that relies on an unhandled exception for failure signaling.
findings.mitigation: Wrap lines 269-271 in try/except jsonschema.ValidationError as e: emit_error(f'index schema validation failed after aggregation — this is a 023C implementation bug: {type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:400]}'); sys.exit(1). This annotates the failure directly in the GitHub Actions summary panel, matching the pattern already established at line 105. File as TF-023C-006.

findings.claim: docs/DECISIONS.md table lists D-042 (line 70) before D-041 (line 71), reversing the ascending ID sequence for two entries that share the same date (2026-05-03). D-041 was filed for slice 023B (emitter) and D-042 for slice 023C (aggregator); within the same date the IDs should appear in ascending order.
findings.evidence: docs/DECISIONS.md line 3 Last Updated: '2026-05-03 (D-042 filed at WP-SCP-023 023C...)'. Table rows: line 70 begins '| D-042 | 2026-05-03 |'; line 71 begins '| D-041 | 2026-05-03 |'. All preceding pairs (D-039/D-040, D-037/D-038, etc.) appear in ascending ID order.
findings.mitigation: Swap lines 70 and 71 so D-041 appears before D-042, restoring ascending ID order.

self_reported_concerns: Action SHA pin verification: The workflow uses SHA-pinned action references for actions/checkout v6.0.2 (de0fac2e...), actions/setup-python v6.2.0 (a309ff8b...), actions/upload-artifact v7.0.1 (043fb46d...), actions/download-artifact v8.0.1 (3e5f45b2...), and peter-evans/create-pull-request v8.1.1 (5f6978fa...). STATUS.md lines 96-99 confirm Dependabot merged four of these version bumps on 2026-05-02 (one day before this commit), providing indirect corroboration for the version-comment accuracy. However, I cannot independently verify the SHA-to-tag mappings without network access to the respective GitHub repos. These should be verified by the orchestrator against the tagged releases before merge.

gh run download --name behavior: The aggregator assumes that gh run download with --name scorecard-emit --dir <tmp> extracts scorecard-emit.json directly to <tmp>/scorecard-emit.json (not <tmp>/scorecard-emit/scorecard-emit.json). Per GitHub CLI documentation, specifying --name for a single artifact extracts files directly to --dir without creating a subdirectory — so the path at workflow line 200 should be correct. However, this assumption cannot be verified from static analysis alone. If the gh CLI version on ubuntu-24.04 creates a subdirectory when --name is given, every adopter would receive no_emit: 'scorecard-emit.json missing from downloaded artifact' and the aggregator would be functionally inert. The STATUS.md 023C entry reports 11/11 pytest pass, but those tests do not exercise the runtime gh run download path. Recommend verifying by running the aggregator against the SCP self-dogfood once self-dogfood opt-in (TF-023C-001) is addressed.

attestations: read permission: The aggregate job declares 'attestations: read' to support gh attestation verify. I believe this is the correct GitHub Actions permission for reading the Artifact Attestation API, added with the attestation feature. However, I cannot confirm from static analysis whether this permission is strictly required, whether it is a recognised permission name in all GitHub Actions runner versions, or whether the default github.token already carries sufficient implicit attestation read access. If attestations: read is unrecognised, it would be silently ignored by GitHub Actions, meaning the permission set is functionally equivalent to contents: read + actions: read only. This does not create a security regression but is worth verifying.
summary: The 023C aggregator implementation is architecturally correct: mandatory gh attestation verify --signer-workflow enforcement (closing D-042 / 023A MAJ-SAFE-R2-001), two-job permission split (aggregate read-only + commit write-scoped), fail-loudly failure recording for all four status types, waiver content exclusion enforced by schema additionalProperties: false at every level, sort_keys=True for deterministic output, stable artifact name handoff (scorecard-index), correct peter-evans/create-pull-request scoping (add-paths: output/scorecards/index.json only), VERSIONING.md internal-surface enumeration correctly extended, STATUS.md 023C row present, D-042 decision row present with correct Last Updated, and 11/11 pytest tests correctly structured across 6 fixture directories with matching expected-validation-result.txt files. Two MAJ findings require resolution before merge: (1) scorecard-index.schema.json lacks if/then/else conditional validation — all 'Present iff status == X' invariants documented in field descriptions are not machine-enforced, allowing semantically wrong schema-valid index rows; (2) the status enum description maps unreachable and no_emit to the wrong code paths relative to the implementation, and the description of last_emit_run_id / last_emit_commit as 'Present iff status in (verified, verification_failure)' is contradicted by code that sets these fields before determining download-failure status. Three MIN findings cover missing unreachable and no_emit index fixtures, silent last_emit_commit omission on SHA mismatch, and missing emit_error annotation on index schema validation failure. One nit covers D-042/D-041 ordering in the DECISIONS.md table.
